title: State of the Feed — Week of July 20–26, 2026
content_html:
Eight aggregation runs completed this week, collecting 8,280 articles with 560 articles advancing through quality filtering. The ai-tech category dominated ingestion at 107 articles, followed by news at 200 articles before filtering. Local content represented 59 articles post-filtering, wellness and science each contributed 56–60 articles, climate yielded 38 articles, and remaining categories accounted for 48 articles combined. The dimensional scoring model applied standard weighting across quality (0.25), relevance (0.55), and local factors (0.20).

Pipeline efficiency registered a mean noise-to-signal ratio of 1.98 across the 15-run evaluation window, indicating that approximately two fetched articles were required to deliver one filtered result. Range variance from 1.23 to 2.74 remained within acceptable operational parameters, with no efficiency degradation noted. Three new feeds entered the active subscription: Information Bulletins – BC Wildfire Service, Vancouver Sun, and blog.bgcarlisle.com, each scoring above 64.0 in discovery evaluation.

One feed, LoRaMeshDevices, reported errors during the evaluation period and requires technical review. Top discovery candidates for potential inclusion remain Information Bulletins – BC Wildfire Service (73.0), Vancouver Sun (65.1), and Municipal News Archives: My Cariboo Now (64.2), all exceeding threshold parameters for future consideration.

Calibration

KnobOldNewRationale
limits.min_claude_score1820User feedback threshold_sweep shows min_claude_score=20 would cut 28.5% of bad articles while losing only 5.9% of good articles—a favorable trade given the 63.3% overall bad rate. Current value of 18 (raised July 19) is an improvement but insufficient: we're still passing far too many bad articles (band_precision shows even 40-59 composite scores are 54.8% bad). Final feed sizes average 353/run, well above the ~100 target, confirming we have capacity. The previous raises (13→16→18) were conservative steps; user feedback now provides clear evidence to move to the calibration ceiling. This directly addresses the verified quality issue without risking feed scarcity.
